items.question: How does Xether prevent out-of-memory crashes on multi-GB datasets?
items.answer: All pipeline transforms compile to Polars LazyFrame streaming queries paired with DuckDB 2.0 out-of-core disk spill (DUCKDB_TEMP_DIR). Artifacts >=25 MB stream straight to S3 via multipart upload with incremental SHA-256 hashing.

items.question: How is multi-tenant isolation enforced across compute and storage?
items.answer: Every tenant database table enforces PostgreSQL FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY bound to session app.current_org_id, paired with hashed xth_live_ API keys, Redis jti revocation, and strict [org_id]/ S3 prefix scoping.

items.question: What happens if a worker restarts mid-pipeline?
items.answer: NATS JetStream pull workers send msg.in_progress() heartbeats and persist deterministic S3 stage checkpoints. Restarts resume cleanly from the last committed stage without recomputing completed transforms.

items.question: Can we connect Postgres, Snowflake, or internal VPC sources?
items.answer: Yes. Enterprise Dedicated workspaces support private VPC / BYOC worker deployments and vaulted credentials for Amazon S3, PostgreSQL incremental watermarks, Snowflake, MinIO, and paginated REST APIs.

items.question: How are compute hours and storage quotas tracked?
items.answer: Execution workers and storage services emit idempotent UsageEvent ledgers reconciled dynamically into org_quotas, powering live quota bars inside your Team Dashboard.
